5.1: No fresh attack-free full-business Host baseline has been executed here.
GrowthV2 batch nonce API is not yet wired through real Growth CLI/business callers.
M06 prefix selection removes these unrelated-map scans, but whole-state clone/root/schema and bounded working-partition costs are not eliminated or given end-to-end touched-state complexity.
5.2: No universal operation identity and budget covers every parser allocation, nested verification, state I/O, retry, recovery, output and cleanup.

Deadline completion no longer revives expired work; worker-owned reservations remain charged until the worker actually exits. Uninterruptible crypto/state/I/O tails do not have an immediate-release guarantee.
Busy exact-frame retries preserve nonce semantics; they do not establish one persistent CPU budget across every network retry.
This change does not complete a full verification-cache key/context/authorization audit.
5.3: Existing shared Node admission/CPU caps limit identity multiplication; two public lanes and separate Cell limits do not implement four reserved, cost-aware global service classes.
No global estimated-cost scheduler with measured-cost feedback and a proved opportunity for every legitimate public candidate is established.
Existing recovery accepts matching pre-existing local operation capabilities; this patch introduces no remotely self-selected recovery priority, identity preference or paid consensus voting power.
Local queue Busy is retryable and remains distinct from protocol invalidity; bounded hardware/arrival-rate liveness is still unproven.
5.4: Original 4,000 ms / 16 hostile W1 producer Host campaign was not run locally; supplementary 30 s / 24 producers cannot replace it.
All six workload scenarios still require current-source Host observations with failed, cancelled, timed-out and unresolved operations included.
Node selected Rust controls did not execute after the final compiler failure; Python readers and historical 130-attempt fixtures are not live service evidence.
